narrative.overview:
The gallery is a pro shop's racquet wall. Every frame stands upright at one true scale in a row of bays, sectioned by brand under a sign, standing on a shelf rail with a hang-tag label beneath. The comparison is the point: head shape, beam and colourway read because the neighbours are right there at the same size. The interface is the wall, the rail and the type; it never competes with the racquets.
 The page has no colour of its own. Its ground is a mid-light warm grey chosen so black frames and white frames both read against it, and its only chromatic moments come from the racquets: their renders, the swatch mark that slides along the rail on hover, the swatch chip in the spec sheet. Detail is a second room of the same shop: the racquet taken off the wall, turning slowly, with its spec tag set beside it.
keyCharacteristics: One warm-grey ground, one ink, no accent: the catalogue's colourways are the palette.
Racquets at one shared scale, upright, never cropped, never boxed.
Archivo across the board, its width axis doing the work: condensed for labels and model names, wide for the wordmark.
Flat. Depth comes from the 3D renders and nothing else.
One signature motion: the turn on hover or focus, off under reduced motion.

rules.name: The Borrowed Colour Rule
rules.body: The page owns no hue. Any colour on screen comes from a racquet's `swatch` or its render; a new accent would compete with the content.

rules.name: The Two-Frame Test Rule
rules.body: Any ground change must keep both a near-white and a near-black frame clearly separated from it. That is what fixed the wall's value.

rules.name: The One Family Rule
rules.body: Archivo's width axis is the hierarchy. Don't add a display face; reach for wdth and weight.

rules.name: The Code Is Mono Rule
rules.body: Monospace marks things a developer will type: part names, file names, hex values. Nothing else.

rules.name: The Renders Carry Depth Rule
rules.body: If an element needs a shadow to be noticed, it is competing with the racquets. Use ink weight or a Wall Shadow tint instead.

dos: **Do** draw every racquet at the same scale and upright; frame by height.
**Do** take colour only from racquet swatches and renders.
**Do** keep 3D in at most two WebGL contexts: one shared offscreen renderer for all bays, one for the detail view.
**Do** give every 3D state a flat-silhouette fallback in the swatch colour.
**Do** use the width axis of Archivo for hierarchy, tabular numerals for specs.
donts: **Don't** show brand logos, wordmarks or string stencils anywhere; names are plain text.
**Don't** add an accent colour, a dark mode painted by category, or neon tennis-ball yellow.
**Don't** put racquets in cards, boxes or shadowed tiles.
**Don't** add eyebrow labels above headings or a second motion effect that competes with the turn.
